description:
Hi everyone! Flare Chronos is tackling active fire data harmonization using NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite streams. We aim to deliver a practical tool for environmental monitoring and fire history analysis. 
Team is full.
summary: Flare-Chronos is a 26-year cross-sensor (MODIS + VIIRS) harmonized Burning Activity Calendar and Dual-System Cognitive AI Harness. It turns 25+ years of heterogeneous satellite active-fire observations from NASA FIRMS into a single, physics-calibrated, and sensor-invariant record to eliminate artificial trends caused by satellite constellation expansions.
details:
Challenge Selected: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots

Our Solution: The satellite active-fire record spanning 2000–2026+ is highly fragmented across multiple sensors (MODIS on Terra/Aqua, VIIRS on Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21). These sensors have incompatible spatial footprints, varying radiometric calibrations, and different orbital coverages. Naively summing these detections creates artificial upward trends (e.g., the introduction of SNPP in 2012 or NOAA-20/21 in later years).

Flare-Chronos resolves this fragmentation through a rigorous 6-step physics-based harmonization pipeline:

Physical Footprint Reconstruction: We rebuild the instantaneous elliptical footprints from scan angles (correcting MODIS bow-tie distortion and handling VIIRS 3-zone aggregation).
H3 Fractional Allocation: We distribute the energy into the Uber H3 discrete global grid (Res 7 / Res 8) using energy-conserving allocation.
Astronomical Day/Night Unification: We strictly reclassify day/night based on the astronomical Solar Zenith Angle (SZA < 85°).
Noise Rejection: We filter out South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) cosmic-ray spikes and static thermal sources utilizing a unified Probability of Fire, P(fire).
Two-Stage FRP Calibration: We apply a scan-angle observation operator followed by stratified quantile mapping (Aqua → SNPP) to calibrate Fire Radiative Power (FRP).
Spatio-Temporal Deduplication & Normalization: We cluster multi-satellite overpasses into "Fire Episodes" (60-minute windows) and normalize the data by Effective Observation Effort (Ω).

The final output is the Burning Activity Calendar—a 26-year × 73-pentad matrix detailing Harmonized Fire Density (HFD), Harmonized Radiative Flux (HRF), and the Standardized Fire Anomaly Index (SFAI).

Live demo: https://flare-chronos.resonance.io.vn/ — interactive Next.js workbench with the 3D overpass globe, H3 heat calendar, and the dual-system LangGraph harness.
